messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Confidence Intervals calculation
parts:
> > How did the standard error and 95% CI were calculated on the table 5.5,
> > page 166 of the Distance Sampling book (edition 1993)?

The ci was obtained using the log-based interval on pp88-89, with z=1.96.
(The Satterthwaite method, used in Distance, was not used here.) se's for
the 'all' option are found by using the fact that the variance of the sum
is the sum of the variances when the estimates are
independent. e.g. 103.5^2 = 24.7^2 + 100.5^2

Steve Buckland
